cards.prompt: Which Rust types are used together here to get interior mutability for shared linked list nodes?
Why wrap each node in RefCell inside an Rc?
options: Rc allows shared ownership, RefCell allows mutation through shared references
cards.answer: Rc gives multiple owners; RefCell lets you mutate the node even through shared access.

cards.prompt: In this list, the head is a sentinel node whose val is ____.
Explain like I'm 10: how does push find where to add a new item in this linked list?
cards.answer: It starts at the head and keeps following next links node by node. When it finds a node whose next is empty, that is the end, so it attaches the new node there.

cards.prompt: What condition ends the traversal when finding the last node?
cards.answer: The last node is the one whose next is None.

items: Start prev at the head sentinel
Look at the next of curr
If curr.next is None, cut prev.next
cards.answer: It walks with prev and curr and cuts prev.next when curr is the last node.

cards.prompt: Which Rust method reads a node value through RefCell in a shared way?
cards.answer: borrow() gives shared read access; borrow_mut() gives mutable access.

cards.prompt: Because of the head sentinel with None value, converting the list to a Vec skips the head.
cards.answer: The into conversion starts from head.next, so the sentinel is skipped.

cards.prompt: You get a runtime panic that says already borrowed in code using Rc<RefCell>. What is the likely cause in terms of RefCell rules?
cards.answer: RefCell checks borrow rules at runtime: a mutable borrow while another borrow is active panics. Clone the next pointer and drop the borrow first.
